candidates.name: Duomo
candidates.price: Cathedral: adult €3; roof by stairs €13, by lift €15; Baptistery of St John €3
candidates.content: Massive, impressive and slightly mad: the cathedral is a late Gothic confection in white marble, festooned with spires and statues. You can admire the facade free from the piazza; getting inside or onto the roof involves three sep

candidates.name: Museum of the 20th Century
candidates.price: Full admission €10, reduced admission €5, children 0–12 years free; first Sunday of the month, and first and third Tuesdays of the month from 2PM are also free
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri Sat Sun 10:00–19:30, Thu 10:00–22:30
candidates.content: "Del 900" but meaning "since 1900", this modern art museum has a rich selection of works by Modigliani, Picasso, Morandi, Boccioni and more. The upper stairwell gives a good view of the Duomo rooftop.

candidates.name: Brera Art Gallery
candidates.content: One of Italy's most important art collections and one of the foremost collections of Italian paintings. The ticketing system is a bit unusual – there are no "standard" single-entry tickets, only a "Brera card", which allows one to

candidates.name: Scala Theater Museum
candidates.price: €12 (reduced for students and people older than 65)
candidates.content: A museum dedicated to one of the world's most famous opera houses. All types of memorabilias like dresses and pictures are on display. This includes a view into the opera hall from one of the loges, which is a short and simple alt

candidates.name: Bagatti Valsecchi Museum
candidates.price: €14; entrance is included in the Case Museo (house museums) card
candidates.content: Extraordinary, somewhat bizarre 1880s house museum of the aristocratic Bagatti Valsecchi brothers, showcasing their passion for Renaissance art and design. Slightly spoiled by unsympathetic electrical wiring and noise-generating m

candidates.name: Poldi Pezzoli Museum
candidates.price: €15, or included with the Casa Museo card
candidates.content: A varied collection of art from the 14th to 19th century, including armour, clocks, porcelain and tapestries. It has been a museum since 1881. The house was bombed in 1943, resulting in a somewhat incoherent restoration, but the c

candidates.name: Triennale
candidates.price: Adult €10; student, under 26 or senior €8.50; child up to 16 free
candidates.content: Museum of Design and Architecture, always has 4-6 exhibits on the subject of design, photography or modern art, at least 1-2 of which are always free entry.

candidates.name: Saint Mary of the Graces
candidates.content: Houses the famous Last Supper ('Cenacolo Vinciano') by Leonardo da Vinci. It is best to reserve tickets a few months before the visit. Canceled reservations are sold from 08:15 every morning (if there are any, best to show up in p

candidates.name: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
candidates.content: A must-see! A stunning fully frescoed renaissance church. Most of the paintings are the work of Bernardino Luini.

candidates.name: Basilica di San Lorenzo Maggiore
candidates.content: A lovely 4th-century basilica, perhaps is one of the oldest basilicas in Western Europe. It is famous for its beautiful courtyard, with Roman-age columns and statue of the emperor Constantine. The Colonne di San Lorenzo (St. Lawre

candidates.name: Ambrosian Gallery and Library
candidates.content: Historical library that also houses the Ambrosian art gallery with treasures such as Leonardo Atlantic Codex.

candidates.name: Civic Archeological Museum
candidates.content: Roman antiques from Milan and the surrounding area.

candidates.name: Royal Palace
candidates.content: Always hosts many exhibitions, usually very interesting. Tickets are sold separately for each exhibition!

candidates.name: Via Dante
candidates.content: One of the grandest and most frequented fashionable high streets in Milan. The Via Dante, named after the poet, is a beautiful and debonair pedestrian avenue which goes from the busy Piazzale Cordusio, all the way to the Largo Cai

candidates.name: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II
candidates.content: One of the most popular high street shopping arteries in the city. It has a very elegant modern appearance, but too has some well-preserved grand 18th- and 19th-century buildings, including a rotunda-like neoclassical church. The

candidates.name: Via Manzoni
candidates.content: Impressive refined-air street lined with aristocratic apartment blocks and opulent churches. It also hosts the Poldi Pezzoldi museum. Today, it is also one of the city's premier shopping streets, and is noted for containing the Ar

candidates.name: Piazza del Duomo
candidates.content: The grandest square in the city, the Piazza del Duomo is the cultural and social heart of Milan, and contains several of its most famous sights. There's the majestic cathedral and classy Galleria, plus the 18th C Palazzo Reale and

candidates.name: Piazza dei Mercanti
candidates.content: A truly enchanting and tiny medieval square, hidden by the grand palaces in the central part of Milan. Here, in "Merchants' Square" you get lovely Gothic and Renaissance-porticoed houses, and a well right in the middle. At the one

candidates.name: Piazza Belgiojoso
candidates.content: A small, yet very impressive square, which hosts the magnificent neoclassical Belgiojoso Palace, built by Milanese noblemen in the late 1700s, and the House of Manzoni, where notable Italian writer and literary figure Alessandro M

candidates.name: Piazza Della Scala
candidates.content: The location of the Statue of Leonardo da Vinci and La Scala theatre. It is a small, but grand square flanked by fine palaces, such as the city hall and the commercial bank. Great place for a photograph and right next to Galleria

candidates.name: Piazza San Babila
candidates.content: Busy and modern square just north of the cathedral and near the city's fashion district. Architecturally, Piazza San Babila's buildings are virtually all Art-Deco office blocks from the 1930s, but it has a trendy business and cosm

candidates.name: Piazza del Liberty
candidates.content: Small square, which however, is noted for a stunning Art Nouveau palace today called the Hotel del Corso, but once the Trianon. You reach it just off a tiny opening at the beginning of the Corso Vittorio Emanuele.

candidates.name: Castello Sforzesco
candidates.content: "See who's in charge!" The round corner towers of the castle are two fists smacked down on the city plains, while the central square tower stares balefully down towards city centre. Who'd dare challenge the Duke? Yet so confident

candidates.name: Torre Velasca
candidates.content: A tall, huge, castle-like skyscraper built in the 1950s, and one of the first in Italy. Stunning modern architecture. Unfortunately it is not possible to go on top, since it is a private building.

candidates.name: Contemporary Arts Pavilion
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri-Sun 09:30-19:30; Thu 09:30-22:30; Mon closed
candidates.content: A contemporary art space. In 1993 a bomb destroyed the building in a time when Italy was heavily committed in its fight against the Mafia.

candidates.name: Natural Science Museum
candidates.price: Has reduced and free entry (depends on person) after 16:30 most days or 14:30 Fridays

candidates.name: Boschi Di Stefano House Museum
candidates.content: Extensive collection of 20th century art. Building (1929–1931) and some furniture by Piero Portaluppi.

candidates.name: Corso Venezia
candidates.content: Considered one of the finest and most beautiful streets in the city. Right near the glitzy Montenapoleone area, it is flanked by a series of beautiful villas, museums and palazzi, from all eras. It also contains parts of the Giard

candidates.name: Milano Pride
candidates.content: a parade and festival, is held at the end of June each year.

candidates.name: Teatro alla Scala
candidates.content: One of the most renowned opera houses in the world. It first opened in 1778 and re-opened in 2004 after extensive renovation. It has seen performances by stars such as Maria Callas and Pavarotti. Since Italy is the birthplace of o

candidates.name: Watch a football game at San Siro Stadium
candidates.content: Watch AC Milan or FC Internazionale at the famous Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, also known as San Siro, which is shared as a home stadium by both clubs. Tickets for most matches are available in advance or on the day. The rivalry betwe

candidates.name: Sunbathing and do aquatic sports at the Idroscalo
candidates.content: Also known as "sea of Milan", the Idroscalo is an artificial lake in Milan. In this place you can practice many sports such as kayaking, canoeing, dragon boats, rowing, sailing, swimming, horse riding and water skiing. In Idroscal

candidates.name: Teatro dal Verme
candidates.content: Classical music.

candidates.name: Conservatorio di musica Giuseppe Verdi
candidates.content: It is a university for the musicians of the future and concerts by them are held in the Verdi (about 1000 seats) and Puccini halls.

candidates.name: Plastic
candidates.content: a very special club, where he spent a lot of time from Andy Warhol to Giorgio Armani and Dolce e Gabbana. It is located in the coolest area of ​​the city, Milano Sud.

candidates.name: Torre Branca
candidates.content: The tower is 108 m high built in 1933 and designed by architect Giò Ponti. From here you can get good views over Milan.

candidates.name: Auditorium di Milano
candidates.content: The seat of the Verdi orchestra with a program of classical and modern music.

candidates.name: Corteo dei Re Magi
candidates.content: A parade in Milan featuring the Biblical Three Wise Men who visited Jesus on Epiphany.

candidates.name: Bar Magenta
candidates.content: This popular bar is best visited with a bunch of friends during apperitivo, a time when free appetizers are given out, usually around 19:00. It was said that Bar Magenta coined the now very popular “aperitivo”, and having a drink

candidates.name: Dolce e Gabbana Martini Bar
candidates.content: A Dolce & Gabbana themed bar, it is in the posh Venezia avenue, right in the top fashion district. Good place to enjoy a Martini cocktail in Dolce & Gabbana surroundings after some shopping or sightseeing.

candidates.name: Rita
candidates.content: It is the perfect place for a cocktail and Edo, the barman and the owner together with the chief Luca, is the grandmaster. They have strict code for preparing cocktails: no syrups are admitted, only fresh fruit. It is also a perfe

candidates.name: Bar Bianco
candidates.content: It's cash only at this bar, but with Gucci-clad clubbers and their well-suited companions, money seems easy to come by. The life of a party can always be detected in here.

candidates.name: Honky Tonks
candidates.content: Not exactly a country cowboy bar as the name might imply, a more accurate description would include the smoky lounge feel and the jazz music being played. The drinks are well made and they also serve Tex-Mex style food.

candidates.name: Roialto
candidates.content: Its bland façade conceals a real gem of a cocktail bar/restaurant. It is a very popular spot for after-work drinks, or perhaps a pre-club drink if you're going dancing somewhere like the Gattopardo.

candidates.name: Bar Jamaica
candidates.content: A small, trendy and artsy bar in the bohemian Brera district, which in summer times uses its verandah for open-air drinks.

candidates.name: b:free cocktail bar
candidates.content: If you want to visit a real Aperitivo bar in true Italian fashion, this is a worthy hot spot.

candidates.name: Brasserie Bruxelles
candidates.content: A bar specialising in beer from Belgium. 5 beer on draught and 50 in the bottle.

candidates.name: L'Elephant
candidates.content: Wednesday and Thursday nights hosts a gay crowd at L'elephant

candidates.name: Birrificio Lambrate
candidates.content: Features with its own branded beers.

candidates.name: Amnesia
candidates.content: Saturday nights at Billy or Amnesia,

candidates.name: Pianeta Luna
candidates.content: A self service restaurant near the Central Railway Station, with pizza, pasta and other classic Italian dishes and English speaking staff. Very reasonable prices and good food combined with a wide variety of wines - this is not a

candidates.name: Il Canarino
candidates.content: Expect to find typical local dishes on the menu like risotto alla milanese and ossobuco. They have a five courses menu that is a bit expensive but worth the money.

candidates.name: La Ravioleria Sarpi
candidates.content: Maybe the best place to have Chinese dumplings in Italy. Many selections available (pork, beef or vegetarian). They also sell a Chinese version of crêpes. Only takeaway.

candidates.name: Osteria del Gnocco Fritto
candidates.content: At Osteria del Gnocco Fritto the €4.50 cover charge includes baskets of fried hand-size pastries (similar to sopapillas) accompanied by meats, cheeses, or jams (€8-11). The restaurant has a second location further southwest.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Da Giuliano
candidates.content: Nice and cozy pizzeria with great, quite thick and large pizza slices. You can choose your toppings and after a few minutes you'll get your slice. Wood burning oven and loads of Mozzarella.

candidates.name: Ciripizza
candidates.content: Another very yummy pizza restaurant with reasonable prices. Eat in or takeaway. English menu available.

candidates.name: Luna Rossa
candidates.content: A pizza restaurant.

candidates.name: Spontini
candidates.content: Pizza.

candidates.name: Il panino del laghetto
candidates.content: Sandwiches.

candidates.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele
candidates.content: The mother of all shopping malls: upscale shops in a splendid 19th century palace of a mall, with a stunning mosaic floor, and wonderful glass roof and cupola. Contains boutiques such as Louis Vuitton and Prada, a McDonald's fast-

candidates.name: La Rinascente
candidates.content: A big department store in Milan, right in the centre of the city near the Cathedral and Galleria, and very close to the chic Montenapoleone shopping zone. Here you can get houseware, design and appliances, male, female and childre

december.text: In winter, the city can become cold (often below or around freezing point), and the weather is usually foggy and rainy if not snowy. Contains boutiques such as Louis Vuitton and Prada, a McDonald's fast-food restaurant, a silverware store called Bernasc

Caffè Cova: Founded in 1817, this pasticceria (pastry shop) relocated to the exclusive Montenapoleone street in 1950, and is a good place for a cake/tart with a hot drink, such as coffee. At Christmas, enjoy the traditional Panettone cake.
